requirements.text: In case of non-replaceable LED modules, the ESA that is (part of) the light source shall be shown, by a Technical Service test report, not to be mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128; otherwise R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED module interface and fixing geometry against R37/R99/R128 light source categories and confirm the Technical Service non-interchangeability report.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable LED light source, the ESA that is (part of) the light source shall carry an approval number according to Regulation No. 128 (or No. 37 / No. 99); otherwise R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Verify that a valid R128 approval number exists for the LED light source and that it is marked on and matches the fitted light source.

requirements.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA (the rear lamp with its LED modules on PCB) conforming to a type approved under UN R10. The mark need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle (paragraph 5.5).
requirements.test_case: Inspect production samples and drawings to confirm the UN R10 approval mark is present on the lamp.

requirements.text: The UN R10 approval mark on the ESA shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking on the lamp for the circled "E" followed by the correct country number.

requirements.text: The UN R10 approval mark on the ESA shall comprise, to the right of the circle, the number of this Regulation (10) followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "10R-" followed by the assigned approval number, placed to the right of the circle.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear combination lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC design and verify compliance through the full set of R10 ESA tests.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions and for conducted emissions.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the test plan and report cover the Annex 7/8 radiated emission tests and the Annex 10 conducted transient emission test.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and for immunity to conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the test plan and report cover the Annex 9 radiated immunity test and the Annex 10 conducted transient immunity test.

requirements.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7 (broadband emission of ESAs), the broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz, Appendix 6) and a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emission per Annex 7 from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare with the Appendix 6 limit line.

requirements.text: The broadband emission values measured on the ESA representative of its type, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the ESA broadband type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that every measured broadband reading is below the limit across 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: In case the LED driver includes an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency above 9 kHz (e.g. switch-mode/PWM driver or microcontroller), the narrowband limits measured by the method of Annex 8 shall be 52 to 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz, Appendix 7) and a constant 53 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emission per Annex 8 with an average detector from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare with the Appendix 7 limit line.

requirements.text: In case the LED driver includes an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz, the narrowband emission values measured on the ESA representative of its type, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the ESA narrowband type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all narrowband readings are below the limit across 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: In case the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz (passive resistor/linear LED drive), the ESA shall be deemed to comply with the narrowband limits of paragraph 6.6.2 and Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Review the schematic and component data to confirm no oscillator or clock above 9 kHz is present.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances by the ESA on its 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 and shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes of Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emission on the supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare the peak pulse amplitudes with Table 1.

requirements.text: Maximum allowed transient pulse amplitude emitted on the supply lines: for 12 V systems, positive +75 V and negative -100 V; for 24 V systems, positive +150 V and negative -450 V.
requirements.test_case: Check the recorded positive and negative pulse amplitudes against the limits for the applicable supply voltage.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is not switched, contains no switches and does not include an inductive load, the ESA need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit design for switches and inductive loads to decide whether the exception applies.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation shall be tested by method(s) from Annex 9 at the test severity of Table 2a over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band and at no less than the minimum test level of Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 9 radiated immunity test at the Table 2a/2b levels for the chosen method.

requirements.text: Radiated immunity test levels over more than 90 per cent of the band: stripline 60 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Verify that the applied field strength or current meets the Table 2a level over more than 90 per cent of the frequency points.

requirements.text: Minimum radiated immunity test levels over the whole band: stripline 50 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 62.5 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Verify that the applied level never falls below the Table 2b minimum at any test frequency.

requirements.text: During the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity-related functions of the ESA (stop lamp and rear position lamp).
requirements.test_case: Monitor stop lamp and rear position lamp light output (e.g. camera or photodetector) during exposure and confirm there is no switching off, flicker or intensity change.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, at the test levels of Tables 3a and 3b and meeting the functional status classifications given there.
requirements.test_case: Apply the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses to the lamp supply lines and assess functional status per ISO 16750-1 / ISO 7637-1.

requirements.text: In case the ESA can be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor: starting profile at level II (12 V and 24 V), 10 pulses. Required functional status for immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp): class B if the function shall be operational during engine start phases, otherwise class C. Required status for functions not related to immunity (reversing lamp): class D.
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 ISO 16750-2 level II starting profile pulses and verify the lamp functions reach the required status class.

requirements.text: Conducted transient immunity: pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V) / -450 V (24 V) for 500 pulses, FPSC III; pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V) for 500 pulses, FPSC I for immunity-related functions and III otherwise; pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V) / +20 V (24 V) for 10 pulses, FPSC II for immunity-related functions and III otherwise; pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V) / -150 V (24 V) for 1 h, FPSC I for immunity-related functions and III otherwise; pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V) / +150 V (24 V) for 1 h, FPSC I for immunity-related functions and III otherwise. The immunity-related functions are the stop lamp and rear position lamp; the reversing lamp is not immunity-related.
requirements.test_case: Apply each ISO 7637-2 pulse at the level for the applicable supply voltage and verify the stop lamp, position lamp and reversing lamp meet their required FPSC.

requirements.text: The rear combination lamp (ESA) approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
requirements.test_case: Take production samples and repeat the paragraph 6 ESA emission and immunity tests (Annexes 7, 8, 9, 10), comparing results with the type approval report.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (or where the emission tests are not waived under paragraph 6.10), the broadband electromagnetic disturbance levels measured on a production lamp shall not exceed the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of a series lamp per Annex 7 and check that every level is at most 4 dB above the paragraph 6.5.2.1 limit.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (or where the emission tests are not waived under paragraph 6.10), the narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels measured on a production lamp shall not exceed the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.6.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions of a series lamp per Annex 8 and check that every level is at most 4 dB above the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limit.

requirements.text: A production lamp shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle that could be observed by the driver or other road users (e.g. stop lamp or rear position lamp switching off, or the stop lamp activating unexpectedly) when subjected to an electromagnetic field strength (V/m) of up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Run the Annex 9 radiated immunity test on a series lamp at 80 per cent of the paragraph 6.8.2.1 levels while monitoring the stop and rear position lamp outputs for any degradation.

requirements.text: A production lamp shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) when subjected to conducted transient disturbances on the 12 V or 24 V supply lines up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1 (ISO 7637-2 test pulses per Annex 10), for the rated supply voltage of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 7637-2 pulses of paragraph 6.9.1 to the supply lines of a series lamp per Annex 10 and verify the functional status of the stop and rear position lamp functions.

requirements.text: The conducted transient emission of a production lamp on the 12 V or 24 V supply lines shall not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1 (maximum allowed pulse amplitude per Annex 10), for the rated supply voltage of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the switching transients of a series lamp per ISO 7637-2 / Annex 10 and compare the peak amplitudes with the paragraph 6.7.1 limits.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth: E = 62 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m for 30-75 MHz; E = 52 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m for 75-400 MHz; E = 63 dBµV/m for 400-1,000 MHz. In case of a passive LED drive (resistors/linear only, no oscillator or switching), this applies unless the exceptions of paragraph 6.10 relieve the broadband emission test.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of the lamp per Annex 7 (ALSE, 120 kHz bandwidth, peak detector) from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare against the Appendix 6 limit curve.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth: E = 52 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m for 30-75 MHz; E = 42 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m for 75-400 MHz; E = 53 dBµV/m for 400-1,000 MHz. In case of an active electronic driver (switch-mode/PWM or microcontroller with clock oscillator), this narrowband test applies. In case of a passive drive without an oscillator, it applies unless the exceptions of paragraph 6.10 relieve it.
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions of the lamp per Annex 8 (ALSE, 120 kHz bandwidth, average detector) from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare against the Appendix 7 limit curve.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated in Annex 7, the rear lamp ESA (LED modules on PCB with drive circuitry) shall be tested for broadband electromagnetic emissions according to CISPR 25, so that compliance with the broadband limits of paragraph 6.5 can be shown. In case of a passive LED drive (resistors/linear only), this applies unless the exception of paragraph 6.10 is claimed.
requirements.test_case: Perform a CISPR 25 broadband radiated emission test on the complete lamp and compare the results with the paragraph 6.5 limits.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall comply with the broadband emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz when measured in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan the full 30–1,000 MHz range in horizontal and vertical polarisation and check that all readings are below the paragraph 6.5 limit line.

requirements.text: For the rear lamp ESA, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal and vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurement was made, and this characteristic reading shall be within the limit.
requirements.test_case: Determine the worst-case reading of both polarisations per frequency band and confirm that it is below the applicable limit.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA shall be measured according to CISPR 25, using the ALSE method of paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25 (or an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4), unless otherwise stated in Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform a CISPR 25 ALSE radiated emission measurement of the lamp ESA and review its conformity to the CISPR 25 setup.

requirements.text: The ESA narrowband emission limits of paragraph 6.6 shall be met throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Sweep 30–1,000 MHz in the ALSE and compare all measured narrowband levels against the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: For each of the 14 frequency bands, the characteristic reading of the ESA shall be the maximum of the readings relative to the limit for horizontal and vertical antenna polarisation, and this reading shall not exceed the limit.
requirements.test_case: Measure in both antenna polarisations and confirm that the worst-case reading per band is below the limit.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall comply with the radiated immunity requirements using any combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the full frequency range of 20 to 6,000 MHz is covered: absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell testing (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection testing (ISO 11452-4), stripline testing (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11).
requirements.test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm that the chosen ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz without gaps.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be exposed to the immunity test signal over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the radiated immunity sweep from 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 steps and dwell times, and monitor lamp operation.

requirements.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the test signal shall be amplitude modulated (AM) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth.
requirements.test_case: Verify the signal generator settings (AM, 1 kHz, 80 %) for 20 to 400 MHz in the test report.

requirements.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the test signal shall be pulse modulation type 2 (PM2), with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs.
requirements.test_case: Verify the PM2 settings (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) for 2,700 to 3,100 MHz in the test report.

requirements.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the test signal shall be pulse modulation type 3 (PM3), with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs.
requirements.test_case: Verify the PM3 settings (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) for 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz in the test report.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall be immune to transient disturbances conducted along its 12/24 V supply lines when test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 are applied to the supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the lamp supply lines and verify that the stop, rear position and reversing functions meet the required functional status.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall be immune to ISO 7637-2 test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b applied to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines (e.g. switched function inputs such as stop or position lamp feeds).
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 7637-2 pulses to each function input and connector pin that can be connected to supply lines, and check lamp behaviour against the functional status criteria.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to its supply lines and to other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines, unless the lamp is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the supply and function input lines and verify that the lamp functions meet the required functional status.

requirements.text: The transient conducted disturbances that the rear lamp ESA generates on its 12/24 V supply lines, and on other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines, shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 and limited.
requirements.test_case: Measure the switching transients on the lamp supply lines with the ISO 7637-2 emission set-up and compare them with the applicable limits.

requirements.text: In case the ESA can be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA's behaviour under the starting profile shall be assessed against the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile at level II and classify the stop, rear position and reversing lamp behaviour against the ISO 16750-1 functional status classes.

requirements.text: For conducted transient pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, the ESA's behaviour shall be assessed using the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as defined in ISO 7637-1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 7637-2 pulses and record each lamp function's behaviour, then classify it against the ISO 7637-1 FPSC levels required in Table 3b.

requirements.text: Every lamp of the approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect drawings and a sample lamp to confirm a marking area that can hold all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings on a sample lamp for legibility.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be indelible.
requirements.test_case: Rub-test the markings (e.g. with a cloth soaked in water and with petroleum spirit) and confirm they remain intact and legible.

requirements.text: The dimension 'a' of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension 'a' of the approval mark on the sample lamp or tool drawing.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circle, the letter E and the correct country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the correct sequential number from the approval.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Visually check that the sequential number sits next to the E-circle.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamp functions for which type approval has been granted, as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
requirements.test_case: Compare the function symbols on the lamp with the approved functions.

requirements.text: The function symbols shall be: for the rear position lamp, 'R1' (steady) or 'R2' (variable intensity); for the stop lamp, 'S1' (steady) or 'S2' (variable intensity); for the reversing lamp, 'AR' (the letters A and R may be mingled).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for R1/R2, S1/S2 and AR in line with the approved variants.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time the approval was issued (e.g. '148R01').
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '148R' followed by the correct series digits.

requirements.text: If the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the lamp shall bear a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: Check the design for side-specific mounting and, if so, inspect the lamp for the horizontal arrow.

requirements.text: In case of a side-specific lamp, the horizontal arrow for the rear position lamp shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp as fitted and confirm the arrow points outboard.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp has the reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect the lamp and confirm an outboard-pointing arrow.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter 'D' shall be placed to the right side of the relevant function symbol.
requirements.test_case: For the D variant, inspect that the letter D follows the function symbol on its right.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter 'Y' shall be placed to the right side of the relevant function symbol.
requirements.test_case: For the Y variant, inspect that the letter Y follows the function symbol on its right.

requirements.text: In case the lamp has reduced light distribution (paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the lamp shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect the lamp for the downward vertical arrow on a horizontal segment.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect a production lamp for the complete approval marking.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: Because the lamp has non-replaceable light sources (and possibly electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control), the lamp shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the voltage range.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking, e.g. '12V'.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, each light source module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: For the module variant, inspect the module for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, each light source module shall bear its specific identification code, made of the starting letters 'MD' followed by the approval mark without the circle, plus additional symbols or characters if several non-identical modules are used.
requirements.test_case: For the module variant, inspect the module for the MD code format.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the approval mark in the module identification code and the approval mark on the lamp shall be from the same applicant.
requirements.test_case: Compare the module MD code with the lamp approval mark to confirm the same applicant.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, each light source module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the voltage range.
requirements.test_case: For the module variant, inspect the module for the voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
requirements.test_case: For the module variant, inspect the lamp housing for the module MD code.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the voltage range.
requirements.test_case: For the module variant, inspect the lamp for the voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, that control gear shall be marked with its identification number.
requirements.test_case: For the external control gear variant, inspect the control gear for its identification number.

requirements.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, that control gear shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: For the external control gear variant, inspect the control gear for the manufacturer's name.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part of the lamp (transparent or not) that is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Review the assembly design to confirm the marked part (e.g. lens or housing) cannot be separated from the outer lens.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Check on the vehicle or a mock-up that the approval marking can be seen when installed or with the boot lid open.

requirements.text: If the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: If the lens is detachable, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.

requirements.text: In case the outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each device body to confirm it carries only the marking of its own functions.

requirements.text: The approval marking, the applicant's trade name or mark, the rated voltage marking, the module identification code and voltage marking on the lamp (if modules are used), and the control gear identification (if applicable) shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp to confirm all applicable markings are on the lamp itself.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the markings required on the light source module (trade name, MD identification code, rated voltage) shall be affixed on the module itself.
requirements.test_case: For the module variant, inspect the module component for its markings.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (including grouping with the R150 retro-reflector), that mark shall be visible after installation.
requirements.test_case: With the lamp installed on the vehicle, verify that the single approval mark can be seen.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Review the design to confirm the lens and other light-transmitting parts cannot be removed without removing the marked part.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, the size of its components shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations (e.g. R148 and R150) under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the components of the combined mark against the minimum sizes required by R148 and R150.

requirements.text: The lamp shall meet the requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN R48 (series in force at the time of application) that are pertinent to each lamp function and to vehicle category M1, where verification at lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp against the applicable R48 provisions verifiable at device level, e.g. geometric visibility, apparent surface and colour, by inspection and photometry.

requirements.text: The lamp shall be designed and constructed so that, in normal conditions of use and despite the vibrations it may be subjected to, its satisfactory operation remains assured.
requirements.test_case: Run a vibration test on the mounted lamp, then check that all functions operate.

requirements.text: The lamp shall retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R148 (photometric, colorimetric) in normal conditions of use and despite vibrations it may be subjected to.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometric and colorimetric measurements after the vibration exposure and compare them with the limits.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the circuit and LED layout for separate light sources per function, or check that the tell-tale declaration is made.

requirements.text: In case a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, only one logo, and only that of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer, shall be incorporated in the internal optical structure and/or the outer lens texture inside the apparent surface.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp visually and check the vehicle manufacturer's logo statement.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm².
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected area of the logo's light emitting surface in the direction of the reference axis.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, all photometric and other requirements for the rear position lamp function shall still be fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Carry out the full rear position lamp photometric and colour tests on a sample with the logo.

requirements.text: The stop lamp and the reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the apparent surfaces of the stop and reversing lamps for any logo.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source (or group of light sources wired so that one failure extinguishes all of them) in a lamp function containing more than one light source, and where the lamp relies on internal failure provisions only, the light intensity shall still comply with the minimum intensities of the pertinent standard light distribution table in Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Disable each LED (or LED string) in turn and measure the intensity at the Annex 3 grid points against the minimum values.

requirements.text: In case of a multi-light-source lamp function relying on internal failure provisions, the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded when all light sources are illuminated.
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity with all LEDs lit and compare it with the function's maximum value.

requirements.text: In case the lamp relies on the vehicle tell-tale, the lamp shall produce a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure (per R48 paragraphs 6.4.8, 6.7.8, 6.10.8 etc.) upon failure of any one light source.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of each light source and check that the failure signal output is produced.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is category R2, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically if the variable intensity control fails while the lamp emits more than the R1 maximum.
requirements.test_case: Inject a failure into the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities fall within the R1 limits.

requirements.text: In case the stop lamp is category S2, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category S1 shall be fulfilled automatically if the variable intensity control fails while the lamp emits more than the S1 maximum.
requirements.test_case: Inject a failure into the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities fall within the S1 limits.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved to UN R37, R99 and/or R128 (without use restriction), light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the design documentation and the sample for the light source type.

requirements.text: The light-signalling device shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Run radiated and conducted emission tests (e.g. per UN R10 ESA methods) and check the results against the limits.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the module shall only be fittable in the designated and correct position.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to fit the module in incorrect positions and orientations.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the module shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt removal without tools and check that it is not possible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module construction for access to internal parts without destruction.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), regardless of the use of tools, the module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source or with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Try fitting other modules and approved light sources into each module position.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the photometric requirements of the device shall be met when the module is replaced by another module bearing the same light source module identification code.
requirements.test_case: Swap in another module with the same identification code and repeat the photometric tests.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the photometric and colorimetric requirements shall be met with 13.5 V supplied at the lamp (12 V system); for lamps with non-replaceable light sources/modules or controlled by electronic control gear or variable intensity control, they shall be met when the lamp is operated as specified by the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Supply the lamp at 13.5 V or at the applicant's declared operating conditions during photometric measurement.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each lamp function on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at HV on a goniophotometer for each function.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each lamp function shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Scan the full visible field on a goniophotometer and check the peak intensity against the maximum.

requirements.text: Outside the reference axis, the luminous intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the minimum of paragraph 5 multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure for each direction, or not less than the intensity value specified in that figure.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at all Annex 3 grid points and compare it with the minimum values.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Annex 2, the luminous intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the minimum specified for that function in paragraph 5 (for the reversing lamp, as given in its table).
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity throughout the Annex 2 geometric visibility field.

requirements.text: The provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of luminous intensity shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Check the local intensity variations between grid points per Annex 3.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the maximum intensity when all lamps are lit together.
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity with both lamps lit.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D', it shall comply with the minimum intensity if either lamp has failed.
requirements.test_case: Measure the minimum intensities with each lamp switched off in turn.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked 'Y', the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Measure the photometry and colour with all interdependent lamps operated together.

requirements.text: In case of an R2 rear position lamp or S2 stop lamp, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Drive the variable intensity control through all its states and measure the intensities against the range.

requirements.text: In case of an R2 rear position lamp or S2 stop lamp, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities exceeding the steady (R1/S1) maximum under night-time conditions (day/night systems) or under standard conditions (other systems).
requirements.test_case: Set the control to the night-time or standard condition and measure that the maximum intensity is not above the steady category maximum.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by each function (red for rear position and stop lamps, white for reversing lamp) shall comply with the prescribed colour inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the function in Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates with a spectroradiometer across the Annex 3 grid field.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the light visually or by measurement outside the grid field for abrupt colour changes.

requirements.text: Rear position lamp luminous intensities: in case of R1 (steady), minimum 4 cd (par. 4.8.3.1(a)), maximum 17 cd as a single lamp or 8.5 cd as a lamp marked "D"; in case of R2 (variable), minimum 4 cd, maximum 42 cd as a single lamp or 21 cd as a lamp marked "D"; standard light distribution per Figure A3-I; minimum 0.05 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity on axis, across the Figure A3-I grid and within the Table A2-1 angles, and check against the class-specific min/max values.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of up to 60 cd is permitted for the rear position lamp below a plane forming an angle of 5° downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: Measure rear position lamp intensity below 5°D and verify it does not exceed 60 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the rear position lamp emission against the red chromaticity boundaries.

requirements.text: Stop lamp luminous intensities: in case of S1 (steady), minimum 60 cd, maximum 260 cd as a single lamp or 130 cd as a lamp marked "D", minimum 0.3 cd within the angles of geometric visibility; in case of S2 (variable), minimum 60 cd, maximum 730 cd as a single lamp or 365 cd as a lamp marked "D", minimum 0.3 cd (day) and 0.07 cd (night) within the angles of geometric visibility; standard light distribution per Figure A3-I; geometric visibility per Table A2-1.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop lamp intensity on axis, across the Figure A3-I grid and within the Table A2-1 angles, and check against the class-specific values.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the stop lamp emission against the red chromaticity boundaries.

requirements.text: Reversing lamp (AR) luminous intensities: minimum 80 cd; maximum 300 cd in or above the H-plane, 600 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D, and 8000 cd below 5°D; standard light distribution per Figure A3-V; no geometric visibility intensity requirement.
requirements.test_case: Measure reversing lamp intensity at the Figure A3-V points and in the zones above H, between H and 5°D, and below 5°D, against the limits.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices (reduced light distribution), the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, where a luminous intensity of at least 25 cd shall be satisfied.
requirements.test_case: Measure reversing lamp intensity at 30° inwards and verify at least 25 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reversing lamp emission against the white chromaticity boundaries.

requirements.text: The rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions) shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Compare production samples against the approved drawings, documentation and type-approval test results by inspection and photometric/colorimetric re-testing.

requirements.text: For production lamps, no measured value of the rear position lamp, stop lamp or reversing lamp shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity of production samples at the prescribed points and check that each value is within 20 per cent of the R148 minimum and maximum limits.

requirements.text: For minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of production lamps shall be at least the 20 per cent equivalent values of Table 12: required minimum 7∙10^-1 cd -> 5∙10^-1 cd; 6∙10^-1 cd -> 4∙10^-1 cd; 3∙10^-1 cd -> 2∙10^-1 cd; 7∙10^-2 cd -> 5∙10^-2 cd; 5∙10^-2 cd -> 3∙10^-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of production samples throughout the Annex 2/3 fields, comparing low-intensity points against the Table 12 equivalent values.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1 or R2) shall provide geometric visibility over minimum horizontal angles of 45° inboard and 80° outboard. Where the lamp is mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm, the inboard angle may be reduced to 20° below the H-plane only.
requirements.test_case: Check the apparent surface for unobstructed visibility at 45° inboard (20° below the H-plane if mounted below 750 mm) and 80° outboard, using a goniometer or CAD visibility analysis.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1 or R2) shall provide geometric visibility over minimum vertical angles of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For a lamp installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.test_case: Verify the apparent surface is visible at 15° up and 15° down (5° down if mounted below 750 mm), by goniometric inspection or CAD analysis.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1 or S2) shall provide geometric visibility over minimum horizontal angles of 45° inboard and 45° outboard. Where the lamp is mounted with its H-plane below 750 mm, the inboard angle may be reduced to 20° below the H-plane only.
requirements.test_case: Check the stop lamp apparent surface for visibility at 45° inboard (20° below the H-plane if mounted below 750 mm) and 45° outboard, using a goniometer or CAD visibility analysis.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1 or S2) shall provide geometric visibility over minimum vertical angles of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For a lamp installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.test_case: Verify the stop lamp apparent surface is visible at 15° up and 15° down (5° down if mounted below 750 mm), by goniometric inspection or CAD analysis.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp is also used as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1 or RM2), the lamp shall provide geometric visibility over minimum horizontal angles of 0° inboard and 80° outboard. The minimum vertical angles shall be 15° above and 15° below the H-plane, or 15° above and 5° below for an H-plane mounting height of less than 750 mm.
requirements.test_case: Verify by goniometer or CAD analysis that the apparent surface is visible at 0° inboard, 80° outboard, and 15° up and 15° (or 5°) down.

requirements.text: The angles of geometric visibility in Table A2-1 apply to a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle. For a lamp mounted on the left side, the inboard and outboard angles shall be applied in mirror image.
requirements.test_case: Check that the visibility analysis for the left-hand and right-hand lamp variants applies the inboard and outboard angles in mirror image.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp, the luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage of the required minimum intensity shown in the applicable light distribution figure (Figure A3-I), with the reference axis at H = 0°, V = 0° passing through the centre of reference.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each grid point of Figure A3-I, comparing with the percentage of the Table 4/Table 7 minimum.

requirements.text: The minimum intensities derived from the percentages in Figures A3-I to A3-XV shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.
requirements.test_case: Check that the computed point minima in the photometric evaluation are rounded down to three significant digits.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or the S1/S2 stop lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, its photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Review the declared mounting height and limit downward photometric verification to 5° below H if it is ≤ 750 mm.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value (as a percentage) shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric scan between grid points, checking that intermediate intensities are not below the lowest surrounding grid value.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp, if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for these directions.
requirements.test_case: Visual inspection of the reversing lamp, followed if needed by a fine goniophotometric scan between measurement points against the 50 % criterion.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1/R2) and the stop lamp (S1/S2) shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, giving for each direction of measurement the minimum intensity as a percentage of the minimum intensity required in Tables 4 and 7.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points for each function, against the percentage of the table minimum.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall emit at least the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V at the specified measuring points, expressed in degrees from the axis of reference (H = 0°, V = 0°, horizontal, parallel to the vehicle median longitudinal plane, oriented in the required direction of visibility and passing through the centre of reference).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing lamp at each Figure A3-V point, compared with the cd minima.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall not differ mechanically and geometrically from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Dimensionally inspect randomly selected production lamps against the approved drawings and compare them with the approved sample.

requirements.text: Any mass-produced lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric performance requirements when tested according to paragraph 4.8 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity of a randomly selected production lamp per paragraph 4.8 at the Annex 3 points for each function and compare it with the limits.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps shall comply with the required chromaticity coordinates (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function of a production lamp with a spectroradiometer under paragraph 4.9 conditions.

requirements.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, mass-produced lamps shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimensions and geometry of randomly selected production lamps and compare them with the approved drawings and type sample.

requirements.text: When the photometric performances of paragraph 4.8 are tested on any mass-produced lamp chosen at random (rear position, stop and reversing functions), no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity at the prescribed points for each function on random production lamps and check the values against the paragraph 6.1.3 limits.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by mass-produced lamps (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) shall comply with the requirements when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function on random production lamps under paragraph 4.9 conditions and check them against the colour boundaries.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (AR) using LED (non-incandescent) technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum luminous intensity requirements.
requirements.test_case: Operate the reversing lamp on a goniophotometer and measure (or derive via HV ratio) the intensity distribution after 1 min and 10 min, checking all points against the min/max values.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2) using LED technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum luminous intensity requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the rear position lamp intensity distribution after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and verify every test point lies within the min/max limits.

requirements.text: For the stop lamp (S1/S2) using LED technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum luminous intensity requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the stop lamp intensity distribution after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and verify every test point lies within the min/max limits.

requirements.text: Each lamp function using LED technology only (rear position, stop and reversing) is deemed to comply with the luminous intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to Annex 8 paragraph 1.2 comply; therefore the 1.2 measurements shall be compliant for each function.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that the light source of each function is LED-only and that the 1.2 photometric results comply.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), each lamp function shall meet its minimum luminous intensity requirements at all points in time, starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Record the intensity at the reference coordinate continuously from switch-ON until stability and verify the minimum values are met from the Table A8-1 start time.

requirements.text: Points in time after switch ON and reference coordinates for compliance checking: rear position lamp 4 s at HV; end-outline marker lamp (rear position lamp deemed RM) 4 s at HV; stop lamp 0.2 s at HV; reversing lamp 0.2 s at HV.
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity at HV at 4 s (rear position) and 0.2 s (stop, reversing) after switch-ON and check against minimum requirements.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system partly mounted on a fixed component and partly on a movable component (e.g. tailgate), the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry and colour of the specified interdependent lamp(s) at each fixed position of the movable component across the outboard visibility field.

requirements.text: In case of a 'Y' rear position lamp system partly on a movable component, the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied only if the specified interdependent lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the light distribution grid with the movable component in each fixed position.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of positions, the photometric requirements shall be met for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements with the reference axis set to each declared position or to the extreme positions.

requirements.text: Compliance of the luminous intensities of each lamp function shall be demonstrated by tests carried out according to Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform the luminous intensity tests per Annex 8 (general and additional test requirements) on the approval samples.

requirements.text: Depending on the light source technology, in addition to Annex 8 paragraph 1, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function (rear position, stop, reversing) shall comply with its intensity requirements at the point in time after switch ON listed in Table A8-1, using the reference coordinate of that function given in the table.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the Table A8-1 reference coordinate at the specified time after switch ON, scale the paragraph 1 distribution by the HV ratio, and compare it with the photometric limits.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of an approved type shall have a space large enough for either the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and a sample to confirm a marking area large enough for the full approval marking or UI and the TOP mark.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings on production samples for legibility.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be indelible.
requirements.test_case: Rub the markings, e.g. with a solvent-soaked cloth, and check they remain legible.

requirements.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the dimension 'a' defined in Table 1; for a retro-reflector for motor vehicles of Class IA (independent) or Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight), the minimum value of 'a' is 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the approval mark circle diameter or 'a' dimension and confirm it is at least 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circled 'E' and the correct country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the sequential number and check it against the approval certificate.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking layout for the position of the sequential number relative to the circled E.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbol identifying the retro-reflective device: 'IA' if the housing is watertight (independent Class IA), or 'IB' if the retro-reflector is combined with other signal lamps that are not watertight (Class IB).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the class symbol that matches the approved class.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the Regulation number followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits of the series of amendments in force when the approval was issued (e.g. '150R01').
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '150R' followed by the correct series digits.

requirements.text: If the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the UI mark shall follow the format of Figure I.
requirements.test_case: Compare the UI mark on the part with the format of Figure I.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: If an indication is needed to determine without ambiguity the angle(s) of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer, the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall bear the word 'TOP' inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the photometry depends on rotation; if it does, inspect for a horizontal 'TOP' on the highest part of the illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The approval marking or Unique Identifier, the trade name or mark, and any 'TOP' marking shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the assembled lamp for legibility of all R150 markings.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark or UI is used for the combined rear lamp approved under several UN Regulations (R148 and R150), it may be located anywhere on the lamp only if the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.6.1.1. and 3.3.6.1.2. are met.
requirements.test_case: Review the marking concept for the combined lamp against the conditions.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp, the mark shall be visible after installation on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle (or a buck) for visibility of the mark.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the combined lamp (e.g. the outer lens or retro-reflector insert) shall be removable without also removing the approval mark with the sequential number or UI.
requirements.test_case: Check the assembly design to confirm the mark sits on a part that cannot be separated from the light-transmitting parts.

requirements.text: The components of a single approval mark shall be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the components of the single mark against the minimum 'a' values of R150 and R148.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN Regulation No. 48 (and the annexes they reference), in the series in force at the time of application, that are pertinent to the rear retro-reflector and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied where their verification is feasible at the time of retro-reflector type approval.
requirements.test_case: Review the retro-reflector against the applicable R48 provisions (e.g. colour, shape, visibility-related device features) that can be verified on the device.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and continues to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Verify by passing the full sequence of photometric and resistance tests and inspecting the samples afterwards.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect samples and the design documentation for defects affecting operation or maintenance.

requirements.text: The components of the retro-reflector or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to dismantle the retro-reflector without tools and confirm that the components cannot be easily separated.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer surface and perform a cleaning check to confirm that dirt can be removed easily.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough, and any protuberances on it shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the surface finish and geometry of any protuberances on the outer surface for cleanability.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp as installed and confirm that the inner (prism) surface of the retro-reflector is not accessible.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter (e.g. a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter), the optical unit and filter must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the assembly and attempt separation of the optical unit and filter under normal-use handling.

requirements.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the materials and specifications to confirm that the colour is obtained by mass-tinting and not by paint or varnish.

requirements.text: When the red retro-reflector is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, the angle specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time red colour of retro-reflected light defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflected light under Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and 0° illumination, and compare them with the R48 red limits.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the dimension and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect and measure the retro-reflector shape and dimensions against Annex 5 paragraph 1 (non-triangular shape for Class IA/IB).

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements specified in paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Perform goniophotometric RI measurement and night-time colour measurement per Annex 4 Part 1 and paragraph 4.2.1.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7, depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Run the test sequence of Table 4 (heat, water, fuels, oils, corrosion/rear face where applicable, stability, weathering) and check pass criteria.

requirements.text: At least one hour after the heat resistance test of Annex 6 Part 1, the retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.1.5 and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4 for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, in the positions defined in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
requirements.test_case: Expose samples to the heat test, rest ≥1 h, then check colour and measure RI at 20', β1=β2=0°.

requirements.text: The retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum RI values after the heat test shall meet the complete photometric requirements of paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.test_case: Perform full RI measurement at all angles of Table 3 on the min and max samples.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand the following exposures of the chronological test sequence: heat 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C (Annex 6 Part 1) without distortion; water penetration 10 min in normal position followed by 10 min in inverted position; motor fuels 5 min (Annex 7 Part 1); lubricating oils 5 min (Annex 7 Part 2); stability in time of optical properties (Annex 4 Part 3); resistance to weathering (Annex 6 Part 6); and, where applicable, corrosion 24 h + 2 h interval + 24 h (Annex 6 Part 4) and rear face 1 min (Annex 6 Part 5), each followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Subject sample groups to the listed exposures and durations and perform visual, colour and RI checks after each.

requirements.text: In case the lamp housing is watertight (Class IA), the retro-reflector shall pass the water penetration test of Annex 6 Part 2 and subsequently the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants of Annex 7 Parts 1 and 2.
requirements.test_case: Immerse samples per Annex 6 Part 2 in normal and inverted position, then apply fuel and oil exposures and inspect.

requirements.text: In case the lamp housing is not watertight (Class IB), the retro-reflector shall pass the water test applicable to Class IB (Annex 6, 10 min normal and 10 min inverted position) and subsequently the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants of Annex 7 Parts 1 and 2.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Class IB water test, then fuel and oil exposures, and inspect for damage, colour and RI.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, it shall pass the corrosion test of Annex 6 Part 4.
requirements.test_case: Perform the salt spray corrosion test (24 h + 2 h + 24 h) and inspect, then check colour and RI.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector is mirror-backed with an accessible rear face, it shall pass the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of Annex 6 Part 5.
requirements.test_case: Brush and solvent-treat the rear face per Annex 6 Part 5, then measure RI.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall pass the test for stability in time of its optical properties of Annex 4 Part 3.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate samples per Annex 4 Part 3 and check colour and RI afterwards.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall pass the resistance to weathering test of Annex 6 Part 6.
requirements.test_case: Expose samples per EN ISO 4892-2 as specified in Annex 6 Part 6, then check colour and RI.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions of paragraph 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Visually compare colour and, in case of doubt, measure trichromatic coordinates after each test group.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each group shall have an RI which satisfies paragraph 5.1.4, verified for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at 20', β1=β2=0° after each test group and compare to Table 3 (red: ≥300 mcd/lx).

requirements.text: The manufacturer shall specify one or more, or a range of, axes of reference of the retro-reflector corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of RI values.
requirements.test_case: Check that the reference axis (or range) is defined in the drawings and used for the photometric set-up.

requirements.text: Where more than one, or a range of, axes of reference are specified, the retro-reflector shall meet the RI requirements with reference to each axis of reference or to the extreme axes of the specified range.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements for each declared axis or the extreme axes of the range.

requirements.text: For photometric measurements, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system indicated by the manufacturer, contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter and limited to 100 cm², shall be considered for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Verify on drawings and sample that the declared illuminating surface lies within a 200 mm circle and does not exceed 100 cm²; mask outside areas during photometry.

requirements.text: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the illuminating area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.
requirements.test_case: Check that the perimeter of the area is defined in the approval drawings.

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Annex 4 Part 1, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than (mcd/lx): at divergence 20': 300 at β1=0°/β2=0°, 200 at β1=±10°/β2=0°, 100 at β1=±5°/β2=±20°; at divergence 1°30': 5 at β1=0°/β2=0°, 2.8 at β1=±10°/β2=0°, 2.5 at β1=±5°/β2=±20°.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at each listed angle combination and verify each value meets the minimum.

requirements.text: Within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°), the RI of the retro-reflector shall not be lower than the values specified for those boundary illumination angles in Table 3.
requirements.test_case: Scan RI at intermediate angles within the bounded solid angle at 20' and 1°30' divergence and verify no value falls below the boundary minima.

requirements.text: In case the Class IA/IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values need only be met up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: If low mounting is declared, verify RI at downward angles only up to 5° and confirm the declaration in the approval documents.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector, tested according to paragraph 4.2.1, shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red specified in UN Regulation No. 48 (whether the red colour is produced by the optical unit itself or by the red outer lens acting as filter).
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light with illuminant A per paragraph 4.2.1 and check against the R48 red boundaries.

requirements.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall conform to the approved type from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the shape and dimensions of production retro-reflectors and compare them with the approved drawings and the Annex 5 Class IA/IB requirements.

requirements.text: When the photometric performance of any production retro-reflector chosen at random is tested, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the CIL of random production samples at the prescribed angles and check that each value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced red retro-reflectors shall comply with the prescribed red colour limits.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production samples by colorimetry under the prescribed conditions and check that they lie within the red boundaries.

requirements.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall not differ mechanically or geometrically from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Measure the shape and dimensions of production retro-reflectors and compare them with the approved drawings and Annex 5 Class IA/IB requirements.

requirements.text: When the photometric performance of any production retro-reflector chosen at random is tested, no measured value (CIL) shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors at the prescribed illumination and observation angles and check that each value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: Production retro-reflectors shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed for red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production samples under the prescribed colorimetric test conditions and check them against the red limits.

requirements.text: Production retro-reflectors shall pass the water penetration test described in paragraph 1 of Part 2 of Annex 6.
requirements.test_case: Subject a production retro-reflector (or the lamp containing it) to the Annex 6 Part 2 paragraph 1 water penetration test and verify the pass criteria.

requirements.text: For a retro-reflector not marked "TOP", with an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and an angle of divergence of 20', the retro-reflector rotated about its axis of reference to the position of minimum RI shall conform to the RI value specified in paragraph 5 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the retro-reflector about its reference axis at β = 0°, α = 20' on the goniophotometer, find the minimum-RI position and compare that RI with the paragraph 5 limit.
